transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-21
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Daniel Park (Lumos - Head of Security), Maya Ortiz (Lumos - Cloud Architect), Samir Gupta (Lumos - CTO)

Summary:
Lumos is evaluating Redwood for private inference deployments; primary security questions were around encryption at rest/in transit, BYOK and HSM support, key lifecycle and rotation, audit logs retention and residency. Redwood AE + SE walked through envelope encryption model, BYOK integration options (Cloud KMS CMEK, customer-managed HSM), and private deployment architecture. Action items: share SOC2/ISO docs, BYOK integration guide, schedule deeper technical session for HSM proof-of-concept.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO27001, KMS BYOK, HSM support, envelope encryption, key rotation, audit logs, RBAC/SSO, data residency, Private deployment options

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, appreciate you making time. Quick intros, I'll hand over to Priya for the tech overview then we'll dig into KMS, HSM, and the BYOK ask.
[00:12] Daniel: Thanks Alex, yea uh we're mostly here to understand how Redwood handles keys and whether we can keep full control of root keys in our cloud account. Also log retention and EU-only residency are big for us.
[00:25] Priya: Great, so at a high level, Redwood uses an envelope encryption model. We encrypt data with a data key and then the data key is encrypted with a master key. For hosted mode Redwood manages the master keys; for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed keys via CMEK / BYOK and HSM-backed KMS.
[00:45] Maya: When you say HSM-backed, do you mean you can integrate with our Cloud HSM or we can plug in an on-prem HSM appliance?
[00:53] Priya: Yes both. For cloud customers we support CMEK with AWS KMS/CloudHSM, Azure Key Vault HSM, GCP CMEK. For on-prem or air-gapped we'll support an HSM gateway in the Private deployment where the customer retains root key material - Redwood never stores the unencrypted root key.
[01:12] Samir: Clarify one thing - if we do BYOK, who has access to the plaintext data keys inside Redwood? I know sometimes vendors keep unwrapped copies to speed operations.
[01:23] Priya: Good question. Our design: in BYOK mode we never have access to the unencrypted master key. We use the customer's KMS to unwrap data keys when necessary. The unencrypted data keys live only in-memory on the serving nodes and are evicted per the KV cache TTLs. We can also enable hardware enforced key operations with HSM so unwrap/crypt operations occur inside the HSM boundary.
[01:46] Daniel: So let me play devil's advocate - if you rotate keys on your side, how do we ensure re-encryption of stored artifacts? What's your rotation story?
[01:56] Priya: Rotation is customer-driven for BYOK. If you rotate the master key in your KMS, you can ask Redwood to rewrap existing data key material - we support batch rewrap jobs for stored artifacts. For hosted where Redwood manages keys, we do automated rotation and provide rotation logs and a grace window. We can also support scheduled rewraps as part of maintenance windows.
[02:20] Alex: I'll also add that for Private deployments, the customer can run KMS in their VPC and Redwood's control plane doesn't receive plaintext keys - we only get telemetry and operational signals.
[02:31] Maya: That sounds promising. One compliance note - we require FIPS 140-2 level 3 for certain keys, and our compliance team will demand an HSM with attestations. Can Redwood support an HSM that meets FIPS L3?
[02:44] Priya: Yes, we can integrate with FIPS 140-2 L3 HSMs. For cloud providers, we rely on their HSM offerings which have the certifications; for on-prem we can integrate with FIPS-certified appliances in Private mode. We'll include details in the integration guide.
[02:58] Daniel: What about audit logs? We need immutable logs, tamper-evident, and at least 7 years retention for some records. Also the logs need to show key usage events - who requested unwraps, which service account, IP, time.
[03:12] Priya: Redwood Console exposes detailed audit logs per request, including key usage events. In Private deployment we can ship logs to your SIEM (e.g., Splunk) or an S3 bucket with object-level immutability policy. We support long-term retention; we'll need to confirm the retention SLA and storage cost model.
[03:31] Samir: Encryption in transit - are we using mTLS between our VPC and Redwood? We want mutual authentication, not just TLS.
[03:39] Alex: For Private we can enable mTLS with client certs; for Hosted we use TLS1.2/1.3 with strict ciphers and optional IP allow lists and VPC peering. Priya can send the exact cipher suites and cert rotation process.
[03:54] Maya: A small transcription note I saw earlier - the doc referred to "Redwood Privatee" in the slides, lol, but the architecture diagram is helpful. In Private mode will our traffic ever traverse Redwood's public control plane?
[04:06] Priya: Control plane signals do cross Redwood's managed control plane by default, but we offer an option for a private control plane for customers who require complete separation; with that the control plane endpoints are in your VPC or on-prem. We also provide on-prem bundles for air-gapped deployments.
[04:24] Daniel: If we opt for private control plane, how do upgrades/patching work? We need to make sure we can approve changes and audit every deployment.
[04:33] Priya: We support canary rollouts and provide release manifests for customer review. For Private installs we can perform upgrades in a staged manner and we keep an audit trail of upgrade events. Customers can require maintenance windows and opt-in for upgrades.
[04:46] Samir: Back to KMS - is there any difference between AWS KMS CMEK and using external HSM from a security posture perspective?
[04:54] Priya: Functionally similar but different guarantees: cloud KMS uses HSM-backed key storage and management provided by the cloud vendor; external HSM gives you more physical control and attestation. If you need a dedicated HSM cluster we can integrate via HSM gateway and route all wrap/unwrap ops through it. There is a latency tradeoff to consider.
[05:12] Maya: Latency - for inference workloads we worry about unwrap latency added to the critical path. How do you mitigate that?
[05:19] Priya: We use caching for data keys - unwrap only on cache miss. The serving nodes keep data keys in memory with tight TTLs and we batch unwraps when possible. For high throughput we recommend a Dedicated pool in the same region as your KMS or colocate HSM to reduce RTT.
[05:37] Daniel: Do you have any customers using an HSM gateway in production with low-latency needs? Any numbers on added ms?
[05:44] Priya: Yes a few large customers. Typical additional latency per unwrap is 5-20ms depending on HSM and network; because of caching the per-token impact is effectively zero for warmed caches. We'll share benchmark notes.
[05:57] Alex: I'll include our benchmark spreadsheet in the follow up; that has unwrap numbers and end-to-end P50/P95 for different configs.
[06:05] Maya: Can you briefly describe the entitlement model - RBAC and SSO? We need SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO and per-route role controls.
[06:14] Priya: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC inside Redwood Console. For Private installs you can integrate with your identity provider and enforce the same policies. Audit events for role changes are recorded.
[06:27] Daniel: One of our auditors will ask whether Redwood has SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001. Do you have artifacts we can share under NDA?
[06:35] Alex: Yes we do. I'll share the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO27001 cert, penetration test summary and our data processing agreement after this meeting.
[06:43] Samir: Great. Also two last questions - if we decide to terminate the contract, what's key destruction and data deletion look like? We need cryptographic erasure and proof of deletion.
[06:55] Priya: For BYOK, because you control master keys, destroying the master key in your KMS effectively makes data irrecoverable. For hosted keys we perform cryptographic deletion workflows, zeroization, and can provide deletion certificates and object-level deletion logs. We'll provide the exact playbook.
[07:11] Maya: Ok cool. From a compliance point of view we need evidence of key access logs, HSM attestations, and a way to prove that nobody at Redwood had access to root keys.
[07:22] Priya: We'll bundle the HSM attestation docs and the key access audit extracts. For Private deployments we can also provide proofs that keys never leave your environment.
[07:33] Daniel: Sounds like solid coverage. For next steps we'll want the docs and then a deep-dive PoC on a small workload with our Cloud team to validate latency and the HSM gateway.
[07:42] Alex: Perfect - we'll get the pack out by Monday. Priya, can you lead the PoC planning?
[07:47] Priya: Yep, I'll coordinate with Maya and Samir and propose a runbook.
[07:52] Samir: Thanks everyone.
[07:54] Alex: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the security pack and schedule the technical session.

End of transcript.
